entries.title: Laremy Tunsil’s Injury Deals a Major Blow To the Commanders’ Offense
entries.summary: Washington will have to look inside and out of the organization to find a replacement for the All-Pro tackle.
entries.content:
Commanders left tackle Laremy Tunsil reportedly tore a triceps in practice Saturday, an injury that could sideline the Pro Bowler for months and casts plenty of uncertainty over Washington’s offense.

During a one-on-one pass-blocking drill against linebacker Odafe Oweh, Tunsil engaged with Oweh for a few seconds before bending over in pain. He walked with team staff to the medical tent before heading indoors.

Tunsil’s injury and possible need for surgery, first reported by NFL Network, has not yet been confirmed by Washington. The team has an off day Sunday and will return to practice Monday. Coach Dan Quinn is scheduled to address the media at 8 a.m.

A 2015 study found that players who sustained torn triceps missed an average of 5 ½ months, which would have Tunsil missing all but the final few games of the regular season.

Regardless of timing, the absence of Tunsil, 32, would be a major blow to the Commanders’ offensive line. Long considered one of the best left tackles in the league, Tunsil allowed just two sacks and two hits on the quarterback on 491 pass-blocking snaps last season, according to Pro Football Focus.

The line already entered camp with question marks. Right tackle Josh Conerly Jr. is coming off a rough rookie season (eight sacks and 43 pressures allowed) and there is an active competition between Chris Paul and Brandon Coleman at left guard. Center Nick Allegretti, a converted guard, hasn’t practiced since July 29 while nursing a calf strain. Blocking tight end John Bates has been out since July 30 with a strained hamstring.

Now Washington is tasked with replacing the blind-side protector of quarterback Jayden Daniels, who has been sacked the 13th-most times (65) since 2024 despite playing in only four complete games last season due to injury.

The Commanders have both in-house and outside options to replace Tunsil.

Veteran Andrew Wylie filled in at left tackle in practice Tuesday when Tunsil had an off day and has started at right tackle for both the Commanders and the Chiefs in the past. Conerly played left tackle at Oregon from 2022 to 2024, allowing just two sacks his final two seasons. But moving the former All-American across the line would bring its own complications.

Coleman started 12 games at left tackle during Washington’s run to the NFC championship in 2024 and filled in for Tunsil last season, but he has since been converted to left guard and has even taken a few reps at center during camp. There’s also reserve tackle Trent Scott and new addition Nicholas Petit-Frere, who was signed Saturday.

As far as free agents, the list of available left tackles is headlined by Taylor Decker, who spent time with Commanders coordinator David Blough in Detroit. Former Jaguar Cam Robinson is also available, as is Cornelius Lucas, who played both tackle positions for Washington from 2020 to 2024.

Coleman may have the inside track to replacing Tunsil, because of both his experience at the position and the team’s longtime investment in him.

“We certainly think he has what it takes to be a tackle in this league,” general manager Adam Peters told reporters after drafting Coleman in 2024. “And he’s got the feet; he’s got the speed; he’s got the strength. And he’s got the intelligence, and he’s got the right mind-set.”
entries.author: Martenzie Johnson

entries.title: Abdul El-Sayed Calls Streamer Hasan Piker’s Past 9/11 Comment a ‘Dumb Statement’
entries.summary: The Michigan Senate candidate did not answer whether he plans to appear with Piker again on the campaign trail.
entries.content:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed denounced streamer Hasan Piker’s past comment that America deserved the Sept. 11 attacks, calling it a “dumb statement.”

“Of course it was a dumb statement and of course I think Hasan himself would say that was a dumb statement,” El-Sayed said in an interview with NBC’s “Meet the Press.”

El-Sayed appeared with Piker on the campaign trail ahead of the Michigan primary, triggering a backlash over Piker’s 2019 comment that “America deserved 9/11, dude,” and that we “totally brought it on ourselves.” Piker, a left-wing commentator whose Twitch stream is one of the platform’s most subscribed channels, walked those comments back two days later.

El-Sayed would not answer whether he plans to campaign with Piker ahead of the general election.

“He disavowed it. So yes, America didn’t deserve 9/11, but you know, to sit here and play gotcha politics with a dumb thing somebody said out of context that they disavowed themselves — to say, ‘Oh, well, what does that mean about what you think?’” El-Sayed said. “I want to be held accountable for what I say and what I do, rather than this idea that we’re so stuck in cancel culture that all of us agreed was a bad idea back in 2020, but we seem to want to bring back.”

Earlier this year, El-Sayed told Politico he was “not here to disavow people’s views” when asked about Piker’s 9/11 comment.

The American Israel Public Affairs Committee spent nearly $32 million in an effort to defeat El-Sayed, who has called for an end to unconditional aid to Israel and has characterized Israeli military operations in Gaza as a “genocide.” The day after El-Sayed won the Senate nomination, President Donald Trump accused him of hating Jewish people and Israel, which El-Sayed strongly denies.

“I love and revere Judaism and the Jewish people,” El-Sayed told NBC, adding that he grew up in a community with a large Jewish population. “I am honored in what I got to share with my Jewish sisters and brothers, but they are not the same as AIPAC and Israel.”

El-Sayed said taxpayer dollars should fund Michigan projects rather than “subsidize foreign militaries” abroad, but he also said the U.S. should back Ukraine in its fight against Russia’s invasion.

“In Ukraine, you're talking about attacks from a leader of a neighboring sovereign country who clearly violated international law in attempting to breach the sovereignty of the Ukrainian public. That is conditional on that circumstance,” El-Sayed said. “We have been offering unconditional foreign military aid to Israel, independent of the circumstances, for years and years and years.”

Trump and other GOP officials have started drawing attention to the Democrat’s full name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, in attack ads and speeches. Conservatives used the same tactic with former President Barack Obama by invoking his middle name, Hussein.

“Notice how they chose to use my full name. It echoes exactly what they did against President Obama,” El-Sayed said. “They are going to try to paint me as a certain thing given my name, but I also think it’s important for us to recognize that America has a long history of embracing.”

He said he’d spoken by phone with Obama and hoped the former president would join him on the campaign trail.

El-Sayed will face former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in November.
entries.author: Jenna Monnin
